unit: Ch 11: Ethics and Terms of Audit Engagements
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Meaning of Ethics – A State of Mind
explain: Ethics refers to moral principles that govern an individual's behaviour and actions.
It comes intrinsically from within a person and forms part of their habit and temperament.
Ethics acts as a state of mind to perform duties according to moral standards.
Rules of conduct and moral principles impose binding ethical obligations on individuals.

flow.title: How Ethics Functions in an Individual

topics.example: A businessman chooses to provide genuine quality products even when selling substandard goods could yield higher short-term profits.
remember: Ethics is a state of mind and a science of morals in human conduct.
mistakes: Thinking ethics is just following written legal rules rather than an internal moral compass.

quiz.q: What is the core meaning of ethics in professional conduct?
o: Strictly obeying statutory laws only
Moral principles governing behaviour coming from an intrinsic state of mind
Maximizing profit while avoiding penalties
Following instructions issued by management
quiz.why: Ethics is intrinsically rooted as a state of mind governing moral behavior beyond mere legal rules.

quiz.q: Ethics is best described as which of the following?
o: Science of morals in human conduct
A set of penalties imposed by courts
Commercial trade policies
Financial accounting techniques
quiz.why: The text explicitly defines ethics as the science of morals in human conduct.

topics.title: Need for Professional Ethics
explain: Society, investors, and governments place immense trust in financial statements certified by Chartered Accountants.
The purpose of assurance engagements is to enhance user confidence in reported financial information.
Professional ethics ensure that professionals place the public interest above personal gain.
Adhering to strict self-discipline protects the credibility and reputation of the accountancy profession.
topics.example: An auditor refuses a personal bribe offered by a CFO to hide losses, safeguarding the public interest.
remember: Accepting the responsibility to act in the public interest is a distinguishing feature of the accountancy profession.
mistakes: Assuming professional ethics only exists to protect the auditor rather than the public interest.

quiz.q: Why is professional ethics essential in auditing?
o: To help auditors charge higher fees
Because society reposes tremendous trust in CA services to make financial decisions
To guarantee that companies never go bankrupt
To replace standard accounting frameworks
quiz.why: Society and financial stakeholders rely heavily on CA reports, creating a vital need for trust and ethics.

quiz.q: What is a distinguishing feature of the accountancy profession?
o: Focusing solely on client profitability
Accepting the responsibility to act in the public interest
Guaranteeing absolute accuracy in financial records
Eliminating all business risks for entities
quiz.why: Accepting responsibility to act in the public interest sets accountancy apart as a respected profession.

topics.title: Principles-Based vs Rules-Based Approach to Ethics
explain: Principles-based ethics requires compliance with the spirit of ethical guidelines.
It demands exercising professional judgment in every situation using skill and expertise.
Rules-based ethics strictly follows explicit, written rules, which can lead to a rigid outlook.
Strict rules may overlook the true spirit of ethics and fail to cover all practical situations.
topics.example: When encountering a novel conflict of interest not mentioned in the rulebook, an auditor uses professional judgment to step aside rather than exploiting the loophole.
remember: Principles-based focuses on the 'spirit' of ethics; Rules-based focuses strictly on written rules.
mistakes: Believing that if a specific bad practice is not explicitly forbidden by a written rule, it is ethically allowed.

quiz.q: What is the essence of a principles-based approach to ethics?
o: Strictly adhering to rigid written clauses without interpretation
Complying with the spirit of ethics through professional judgment
Following only legal regulations laid down by statutes
Ignoring ethical guidance when written rules are missing
quiz.why: Principles-based guidance requires accountants to evaluate situations using professional judgment to follow the spirit of ethics.

quiz.q: What is a key drawback of a purely rules-based approach to ethics?
o: It gives too much flexibility to auditors
It can lead to a narrow outlook where the spirit of ethics is overlooked
It relies heavily on professional judgment
It is impossible to enforce legally
quiz.why: A rules-based approach can be overly rigid and cause professionals to ignore the underlying spirit of ethical conduct.

topics.title: Fundamental Principles of Professional Ethics
explain: Integrity requires being straightforward, honest, fair-dealing, and truthful in professional relationships.
Objectivity ensures professional judgment is not compromised by bias, conflict of interest, or undue influence.
Professional Competence and Due Care requires maintaining professional knowledge/skill and acting diligently.
Confidentiality prohibits disclosing client information without authorization, unless required or permitted by law.
Professional Behaviour requires complying with laws and avoiding any conduct that discredits the profession.
topics.example: A CA refuses to sign off on a false financial return requested by a client (Integrity) and keeps client data secure (Confidentiality).
remember: 5 Fundamental Principles: Integrity, Objectivity, Professional Competence & Due Care, Confidentiality, Professional Behaviour.
mistakes: Confusing Confidentiality as absolute; disclosures are allowed when required or permitted by law.

quiz.q: Which fundamental principle requires an auditor to refrain from compromising judgment due to bias or undue influence?
o: Integrity
Objectivity
Confidentiality
Professional Behaviour
quiz.why: Objectivity specifically mandates that judgment must not be compromised by bias, conflict of interest, or influence of others.

quiz.q: When is an auditor permitted to disclose confidential client information?
o: Whenever requested by a friend or family member
When required by law or authorized by the client
Whenever the auditor changes jobs
Confidential information can never be disclosed under any circumstances
quiz.why: Confidential information can be disclosed if required by law, permitted by law with client authorization, or under a professional duty.

topics.title: Independence of Auditors
explain: Independence implies judgment is not subordinate to others' wishes or the auditor's self-interest.
Independence of Mind allows expressing an opinion without compromised judgment, maintaining objectivity and skepticism.
Independence in Appearance requires avoiding facts that would lead a reasonable third party to doubt the auditor's integrity.
Independence must not only exist in fact (mind), but must also be seen to exist by all reasonable persons (appearance).

flow.title: Two Sides of Auditor Independence
steps: Independence in Appearance (Visible Absence of Conflicts)

topics.example: An auditor holds no financial shares in an auditee company (Appearance) and evaluates evidence without personal bias (Mind).
remember: Auditor Independence = Independence of Mind + Independence in Appearance.
mistakes: Thinking legal rules alone can guarantee independence; independence is primarily a state of mind and character.

quiz.q: What is 'Independence of Mind'?
o: Avoiding facts that make third parties doubt the auditor
The state of mind permitting an unbiased opinion without compromised professional judgment
Strictly adhering to legal audit rotation guidelines
Following management instructions without question
quiz.why: Independence of mind is the internal state of mind enabling an auditor to act with integrity, objectivity, and skepticism.

quiz.q: Why is 'Independence in Appearance' necessary?
o: To satisfy reasonable third parties that independence has not been compromised
To reduce auditor work hours
To eliminate the need for written engagement letters
To lower audit fees for the client
quiz.why: Appearance ensures an informed third party concludes that the auditor's objectivity and integrity remain intact.

topics.title: Threats to Independence
explain: Self-Interest Threat: Financial or personal benefits in an audit client (e.g., holding shares, contingent fees).
Self-Review Threat: Re-evaluating own previous non-audit work or judgments during audit (e.g., book-keeping, internal audit).
Advocacy Threat: Promoting client positions to the point of compromising objectivity (e.g., dealing in client shares, litigation defense).
Familiarity Threat: Becoming too sympathetic to client interests due to close relationships or long association.
Intimidation Threat: Being deterred from acting objectively due to pressure or threats (e.g., replacement, litigation, fee cuts).
topics.example: An auditor whose fee depends on client profits faces a Self-Interest threat; an auditor threatened with replacement over accounting policy faces an Intimidation threat.
remember: 5 Threats: Self-interest, Self-review, Advocacy, Familiarity, Intimidation.
mistakes: Classifying auditing internal financial controls previously set up by the auditor as a self-interest threat instead of a self-review threat.

quiz.q: An auditor receiving 40% of their total fee revenue from a single client faces which type of threat?
o: Self-review threat
Self-interest threat
Advocacy threat
Familiarity threat
quiz.why: Undue dependence on a client's fees creates financial reliance, resulting in a self-interest threat.

quiz.q: When an auditor acts as a legal representative for an audit client in a tax court dispute, what threat arises?
o: Advocacy threat
Intimidation threat
Familiarity threat
Self-review threat
quiz.why: Promoting or defending a client's position in litigation creates an advocacy threat to objectivity.

topics.title: Safeguards to Independence
explain: Safeguards are actions or measures taken to eliminate threats or reduce them to an acceptable level.
Before accepting work, auditors must conscientiously evaluate potential threats to independence.
If threats exist, safeguards must be applied and documented as evidence of compliance.
If adequate safeguards cannot be implemented to mitigate threats, the auditor must decline or withdraw from the engagement.
topics.example: Removing a team member whose spouse owns shares in the auditee firm is a safeguard that eliminates a self-interest threat.
remember: If safeguards cannot reduce threats to an acceptable level, the auditor MUST NOT accept or continue the work.
mistakes: Assuming safeguards are optional even when severe threats to independence exist.

quiz.q: What should an auditor do if threats to independence cannot be reduced to an acceptable level by safeguards?
o: Proceed with the audit and issue a disclaimer
Refuse or withdraw from the audit engagement
Charge double fees to cover the risk
Inform the client's internal auditors to handle it
quiz.why: If safeguards cannot adequately reduce threats, the auditor must decline or withdraw from the engagement.

quiz.q: Safeguards are designed to achieve which of the following?
o: Eliminate all audit procedures
Reduce threats to fundamental principles to an acceptable level
Ensure the client makes high profits
Guarantee zero misstatements in financial reports
quiz.why: Safeguards effectively mitigate identified threats to bring them down to an acceptable level.

topics.title: Professional Skepticism
explain: Professional skepticism is an attitude involving a questioning mind and critical assessment of audit evidence.
It requires being alert to contradictory evidence, doubts about document reliability, and indications of possible fraud.
It reduces risks of overlooking unusual circumstances, over-generalizing, or using inappropriate assumptions.
Past honesty of management does not relieve the auditor of the duty to maintain professional skepticism throughout the audit.
topics.example: An auditor notices sales spiking on the last day of the financial year and investigates further rather than accepting invoices at face value.
remember: Professional skepticism is required throughout the entire audit, regardless of past management honesty.
mistakes: Believing that trusting management's integrity eliminates the need to maintain professional skepticism.

quiz.q: Professional skepticism includes being alert to which of the following?
o: Audit evidence that contradicts other audit evidence obtained
Management's request to lower audit fees
The client's market share growth
The personal background of junior staff
quiz.why: Skepticism involves being alert to contradictory audit evidence, indications of fraud, and document unreliability.

quiz.q: Maintaining professional skepticism helps the auditor reduce the risk of:
o: Overlooking unusual circumstances
Failing to collect audit fees on time
Increasing audit staff overheads
Issuing too many engagement letters
quiz.why: Skepticism reduces risks such as overlooking unusual circumstances, over-generalising, and using wrong assumptions.

topics.title: Preconditions for an Audit
explain: SA 210 governs agreeing the terms of audit engagements with management or those charged with governance.
Preconditions require management's use of an acceptable Financial Reporting Framework (FRF).
Management must acknowledge responsibility for preparing financial statements in accordance with the FRF.
Management must acknowledge responsibility for internal controls to prevent material misstatements.
Management must agree to provide unrestricted access to information, additional records, and entity personnel.

flow.title: Establishing Preconditions (SA 210)
steps: Obtain Agreement on FS Preparation Responsibility
Obtain Agreement on Internal Control Responsibility
Obtain Agreement to Provide Full Access & Records

topics.example: Before accepting an audit, the CA verifies that the client uses GAAP/Ind AS and agrees in writing to give complete access to accounts.
remember: Preconditions: Acceptable FRF + Management's agreement on the premise of audit.
mistakes: Accepting an audit when management refuses to take responsibility for internal controls or limits access to records.

quiz.q: Under SA 210, what are the two main elements of preconditions for an audit?
o: Acceptable FRF and management's agreement on audit premise responsibilities
Lowest audit fee agreement and quick completion date
Full insurance cover and guaranteed profit reporting
Audit team rotation and management representation letter
quiz.why: SA 210 defines preconditions as using an acceptable FRF and management agreeing to its basic responsibilities.

quiz.q: Which of the following is part of management's responsibility under the premise of an audit?
o: Designing audit procedures for the external auditor
Providing unrestricted access to all relevant information and personnel
Determining the final audit opinion
Selecting the auditor's engagement team
quiz.why: Management must explicitly agree to provide full access to records, additional information, and personnel.

topics.title: Agreement on Audit Engagement Terms
explain: The agreed terms of audit engagement must be recorded in writing in an Audit Engagement Letter.
The letter avoids misunderstandings regarding the scope and objectives of the audit.
Key contents: Objective & scope of audit, responsibilities of auditor and management, applicable FRF, and expected report form/content.
If law or regulation details engagement terms sufficiently, a formal written agreement is not mandatory except acknowledging management responsibilities.
topics.example: The auditor sends an engagement letter stating reasonable assurance objectives and noting that audit findings might alter the final report format.
remember: Audit engagement letter is sent BY THE AUDITOR TO THE CLIENT to record agreed terms.
mistakes: Thinking the engagement letter is sent by the client to the auditor (it is sent by the auditor to the client).

quiz.q: Who issues the audit engagement letter?
o: The client's management to the auditor
The auditor to the client
The Registrar of Companies to the auditor
The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
quiz.why: The auditor prepares and sends the engagement letter to the client to confirm terms and avoid misunderstandings.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory content of an audit engagement letter under SA 210?
o: Objective and scope of the audit
Identification of applicable financial reporting framework
Guarantee of absolute assurance against all frauds
Reference to expected form and content of auditor's report
quiz.why: An audit provides reasonable assurance, never a guarantee of absolute assurance.

topics.title: Preconditions Not Present & Limitation on Scope Prior to Acceptance
explain: If preconditions are absent, the auditor must discuss the matter with management.
The auditor SHALL NOT accept the audit if FRF is unacceptable or management refuses premise agreement, unless required by law.
If management imposes scope limitations prior to acceptance that would result in disclaiming an opinion, the auditor must decline.
Mandatory statutory audits required by law are exceptions where engagement cannot be outright rejected, but responsibilities must be acknowledged.

flow.title: Decision on Non-Acceptance
steps: Evaluate if Management Agrees to Rectify
If Refused & Would Cause Disclaimer -> Reject Engagement
Proceed Only if Required by Law/Regulation

topics.example: A prospective client tells an auditor they will not allow access to inventory records; the auditor refuses to accept the engagement.
remember: Preconditions absent OR Scope limitation leading to Disclaimer = DO NOT ACCEPT engagement.
mistakes: Accepting a proposed audit engagement despite severe management scope restrictions that guarantee a disclaimer.

quiz.q: What action must an auditor take if preconditions for an audit are not present and management refuses to correct them?
o: Accept the audit and issue an unqualified opinion
Not accept the proposed audit engagement unless required by law
Conduct the audit without checking internal controls
Delegate the decision to the tax authorities
quiz.why: Unless required by law or regulation, an auditor shall not accept an engagement if preconditions are not met.

quiz.q: If management imposes a scope limitation prior to acceptance that will force a disclaimer of opinion, the auditor should:
o: Accept the engagement and modify the fee structure
Not accept such a limited engagement as an audit engagement
Accept and conduct only analytical procedures
Subcontract the work to another audit firm
quiz.why: SA 210 mandates declining engagements where management-imposed scope limits prior to acceptance lead to a disclaimer.

topics.title: Change in Engagement Terms & Recurring Audits
explain: Auditors must not agree to lower assurance terms without reasonable justification (e.g., changed circumstances vs avoiding qualification).
If terms change, new terms must be recorded in writing; if lower assurance is agreed, the report must not reference original audit work.
If unable to agree on terms change and not allowed to continue original audit, auditor must withdraw and report if obligated.
In recurring audits, auditors evaluate whether to revise terms based on management changes, business scale changes, or FRF changes.

flow.title: Handling Request to Change Terms
steps: Evaluate Justification (Reasonable vs Avoiding Qualified Opinion)
If Justified -> Agree & Issue Revised Letter
If Management Refuses Original Audit -> Withdraw & Report

topics.example: A client losing receivables records asks to change audit to review to avoid a qualified opinion; the auditor refuses because justification is missing.
remember: Avoid qualified opinion = NOT a reasonable justification to lower assurance level.
Recurring audits need revised letters if senior management, ownership, or FRF changes.
mistakes: Assuming a new engagement letter must be sent every single year in recurring audits even if no terms have changed.

quiz.q: Which situation represents a reasonable justification for changing an audit engagement to a review engagement?
o: Inability to obtain sufficient audit evidence regarding receivables
A change in circumstances affecting the entity's need for the service
Management's desire to avoid a qualified audit opinion
Disagreements over necessary accounting adjustments
quiz.why: A genuine change in circumstances affecting the need for service is reasonable; avoiding qualification is not.

quiz.q: In recurring audits, which factor suggests a need to revise engagement terms?
o: Routine annual staff rotation in the audit firm
A recent change in senior management or significant change in business size
Completion of audit files within 60 days
Filing of standard tax returns
quiz.why: Changes in management, ownership, business size, or FRF require revising terms or reminding the client of existing terms.

topics.title: Quality Control for Firms (SQC 1)
explain: SQC 1 applies firm-wide to all audits, reviews, assurance, and related service engagements.
It requires establishing a quality control system giving reasonable assurance of compliance with standards and legal rules.
6 Elements: Leadership responsibilities, Ethical requirements, Client acceptance/continuance, HR, Engagement performance, Monitoring.
Documentation retention period: Minimum 7 years from auditor's report date.
Assembly of final engagement file: Completed in not more than 60 days after the date of auditor's report.
topics.example: An audit firm sets up annual written independence declarations for all staff and mandates file assembly within 60 days of report signing.
remember: Assembly of Final File: Max 60 days after auditor's report date.
SQC 1 = Applies to ENTIRE FIRM across ALL engagements.
mistakes: Confusing SQC 1 retention (minimum 7 years) with 6 years.

quiz.q: What is the maximum time allowed under SQC 1 for assembly of final audit engagement files after the report date?
o: 30 days
45 days
60 days
90 days
quiz.why: SQC 1 requires final assembly of engagement files to be completed within 60 days after the date of the auditor's report.

quiz.q: What is the minimum retention period for audit engagement documentation according to SQC 1?
o: 5 years
6 years
7 years
10 years
quiz.why: Documentation for audit engagements must be retained for ordinarily no shorter than seven years from the auditor's report date.

topics.title: Quality Control for an Audit (SA 220)
explain: SA 220 applies specifically to INDIVIDUAL AUDIT ENGAGEMENTS at the engagement level.
It is premised on the firm being subject to SQC 1.
The Engagement Partner takes ultimate responsibility for overall audit quality, direction, supervision, and performance.
The Engagement Partner must ensure an Engagement Quality Control Reviewer (EQCR) is appointed for listed entity audits.
The auditor's report MUST NOT be dated until the completion of the Engagement Quality Control Review.
topics.example: The engagement partner delays signing the audit report of a listed firm until the EQCR partner completes their review and signs off.
remember: SA 220 = Applies to SPECIFIC AUDIT ENGAGEMENT (Engagement Partner responsibility).
Report date MUST NOT precede EQCR completion date.
mistakes: Signing or dating the auditor's report before the mandatory EQCR review is completed.

quiz.q: How does SA 220 differ from SQC 1?
o: SA 220 applies firm-wide, while SQC 1 applies to specific audits
SA 220 applies to a specific audit engagement, whereas SQC 1 applies to the entire firm
SQC 1 applies only to non-audit engagements
SA 220 deals with legal fees while SQC 1 deals with ethical rules
quiz.why: SQC 1 covers all services firm-wide, while SA 220 focuses on quality control for an individual audit engagement.

quiz.q: For listed entity audits, when can the auditor's report be dated under SA 220?
o: Before the engagement quality control review begins
On the day draft financial statements are prepared
Only after the completion of the engagement quality control review
30 days prior to the annual general meeting
quiz.why: SA 220 explicitly prohibits dating the auditor's report until the EQCR process is fully completed.
